trigger.user_message:
# Task: Build Complete Project Context for OrangeHRM Directory Module

Act as a **Senior QA Engineer, Business Analyst, and UI Exploration Specialist**.

Your task is to deeply analyze and document the **OrangeHRM Directory Module** so that this documentation becomes the reliable Project Context for all upcoming QA activities.

## 1. Application Under Test

- Application: OrangeHRM
- URL: https://opensource-demo.orangehrmlive.com/web/index.php/directory/viewDirectory
- Module: Directory
- Scope: UI testing only.
- API testing is explicitly excluded.
- Use the existing project instructions, skills, agents, and documentation standards already available in this repository.
- Do not create unnecessary skills, agents, frameworks, or architecture.

## 2. Main Objective

Explore the Directory module and understand its functionality, UI components, user interactions, business rules, search behavior, displayed data, validation, and possible error states.

The resulting documentation must allow another QA engineer or AI agent to understand the module without having to rediscover its basic functionality.

**Important:** Use the actual running application as the primary source of truth. Do not assume functionality exists just because it is common in HR systems.

## 3. Explore the Module

Use the available browser exploration tools, including Playwright MCP if configured, to inspect the real UI.

First, inspect the current page and identify the available controls.

### A. Directory Page Layout

Document:

- Page title and purpose.
- Navigation path to the Directory module.
- Sidebar navigation and the selected Directory item.
- Search/filter panel.
- Results count.
- Employee cards or result items.
- Employee names and profile images.
- Scrolling behavior and page layout.
- Loading indicators, empty states, errors, and other states if observed.
- Any pagination or additional result-loading mechanism, if present.

### B. Search and Filter Controls

Inspect each control individually.

**Employee Name**
- Input type and placeholder.
- Whether it supports autocomplete or suggestions.
- Whether partial names and full names work.
- Whether it is case-sensitive.
- How the application handles leading/trailing spaces.
- What happens when the input matches no employee.
- What happens when the field is empty.

**Job Title**
- Available options.
- Default selection.
- How the options are populated.
- Whether the selected value can be combined with other filters.
- Search results for selected values.

**Location**
- Available options.
- Default selection.
- How the options are populated.
- Whether the selected value can be combined with other filters.
- Search results for selected values.

**Search button**
- What happens when it is clicked.
- Whether all entered filters are applied together.
- Whether results update immediately or after submission.
- Whether the results count changes.
- How the application behaves when no results match.

**Reset button**
- Which fields are cleared or restored.
- Whether results return to the default state.
- Whether the results count is restored.
- Whether reset works when some or all filters are populated.

Also inspect the filter panel expand/collapse control if available.

### C. Employee Results

Inspect employee result cards and document:

- Information displayed on each card.
- Employee name formatting.
- Profile image or placeholder behavior.
- Whether clicking a card or employee name opens another page or dialog.
- Any additional details revealed by interacting with a card.
- What happens when an employee has a missing or unusual value, if observable.
- How the UI behaves when the number of results is large.
- Scrolling behavior within the results area.

Do not assume that cards are clickable. Verify their behavior.

### D. Search Behavior and Combinations

Explore the supported combinations of:

1. Employee Name only.
2. Job Title only.
3. Location only.
4. Employee Name + Job Title.
5. Employee Name + Location.
6. Job Title + Location.
7. All three filters together.
8. No filters.
9. A value that returns no results.
10. Clearing or resetting previously applied filters.

Use a small number of representative searches first. Expand the exploration where needed to determine the actual behavior.

Do not claim that a scenario passed or failed unless it was actually executed and observed.

### E. UI States and Edge Cases

Investigate where applicable:

- Empty input.
- Partial and exact employee names.
- Invalid or nonexistent employee names.
- Leading and trailing spaces.
- Different letter casing.
- Switching between filter values.
- Repeated Search clicks.
- Reset after a successful search.
- Reset after a zero-result search.
- Long employee names.
- Missing profile images.
- Browser refresh and navigation behavior.

Only report states that you can observe or reasonably verify. Clearly label anything that could not be tested.

## 4. Data and Evidence

For every important observation:

- Record the observed behavior.
- Record the steps used to observe it.
- Capture screenshots when supported and useful.
- Record the relevant page URL.
- Distinguish observed facts from assumptions and unanswered questions.
- Do not expose passwords, tokens, cookies, or other sensitive authentication data in documentation.

Do not invent employee information, dropdown options, result counts, or business rules.

## 5. Documentation to Create

First inspect the existing repository structure and reuse its established locations and formats.

Create or update the following documentation as appropriate:

### `Directory-Module-Overview.md`
Include:
- Module purpose.
- Navigation and page structure.
- Main features.
- Search/filter controls.
- Results display.
- User interactions.
- Dependencies and observed behavior.
- Known limitations and open questions.

### `Directory-Functional-Analysis.md`
Include:
- Detailed behavior of each control.
- Input and selection behavior.
- Search and reset logic.
- Filter combinations.
- Results behavior.
- UI states and edge cases.
- Observed rules versus assumptions.

### `Directory-UI-Inventory.md`
Create a structured inventory of:
- UI element name.
- Element type.
- Location on the page.
- User action.
- Observed response.
- Locator candidates, if inspected.
- Notes or uncertainties.

Do not invent locators. If locator inspection is supported, prefer IDs and XPath for this project's UI automation conventions.

### `Directory-Exploration-Report.md`
Include:
- Exploration date.
- Application URL.
- Exploration scope.
- Areas explored.
- Scenarios actually performed.
- Results and evidence.
- Unverified scenarios.
- Bugs or suspicious behavior observed.
- Remaining questions.

If the repository already has equivalent documents or a prescribed documentation structure, update or reuse those instead of creating duplicate files.

## 6. Project Context Requirements

The resulting Project Context must be useful for future stages:

- Test Design.
- Test Case Review.
- Manual Test Execution.
- UI Automation Generation.
- Automation Execution.
- Defect Reporting.

It must clearly explain what the Directory module does, how its controls behave, what data is displayed, and which behaviors remain uncertain.

Do not generate the final test cases yet. This stage is for understanding and documenting the module.

Do not execute a full test suite. Limited exploratory interactions are allowed to establish the module's actual behavior.

Do not perform API testing.

## 7. Quality and Accuracy Rules

1. Actual application behavior takes priority over assumptions.
2. Never invent functionality, business rules, test results, or evidence.
3. Clearly distinguish `Observed`, `Inferred`, and `Not Verified`.
4. If the application or browser is unavailable, report the blocker instead of pretending exploration succeeded.
5. Reuse the existing project structure and instructions.
6. Keep the documentation clear, structured, and free of unnecessary repetition.
7. Record the work in the existing project journal according to the repository's workflow.
8. Preserve previous files and user decisions; do not overwrite unrelated work.

## 8. Final Response

When finished, provide a concise summary containing:

- Files created or updated and their paths.
- Areas of the Directory module actually explored.
- Important confirmed behaviors.
- Any bugs discovered, without claiming unverified defects.
- Areas not explored and the reasons.
- Whether the Project Context is ready for the next stage.

**Stop after completing the documentation and journal updates. Do not proceed to Test Design or execution until explicitly instructed.**

trigger.reason: Test design requested after EXPLORATION_APPROVED (EVT-0015)
trigger.user_message:
Run the Test Design stage using the approved PRD, Project Context, and Exploration Report v1.1.0.

Decisions:
- Use the existing demo account for this task. Document that coverage is limited to this account.
- Because demo data changes, do not rely on fixed result counts or employee names. Design data-aware tests using currently available records and observable search behavior.

Design positive, negative, boundary, and combined-filter test cases for the Directory UI only. Cover Employee Name autocomplete and validation, Job Title, Location, Search, Reset, result cards, employee details, empty results, scrolling, and relevant keyboard interactions based on the exploration report.

Keep expected results grounded in approved requirements and verified observations. Clearly flag any expected behavior that remains uncertain. Do not test APIs or execute the test cases.

Create the prescribed test-design CSV with exactly these columns:
- `valid in scope`
- `needs automation`

Follow the existing repository conventions for additional test-case fields and review workflow. Update the journal, validate the output, and stop for my review before Test Review or execution.

techniques_used.rationale: The field accepts free text with distinct observed classes: matching partial, case variant, whitespace-padded, non-matching, typed-not-selected, selected suggestion, empty, overlong/special.

areas: PC SA-002/003/006 / filter controls: default vs set state
techniques_used.rationale: Controls have two observed classes (default '-- Select --'/empty vs a selected value); one representative per class covers the reset/default behavior.
Observed boundary in the header wording at result counts 0 ('No Records Found'), 1 ('(1) Record Found') and ≥2 ('(N) Records Found').
Search outcome depends on which of Employee Name, Job Title and Location are set and whether the name was selected.
Observed states closed → open (card click) → closed (arrow icon).
Observed states expanded → collapsed (toggle); the return transition was not evidenced.

areas: PC SA-002 / Employee Name validation message
techniques_used.rationale: Observed states: no message → 'Invalid' (Search with unselected text) → still 'Invalid' (retyping) → cleared (suggestion selected).
Observed states: initial batch (14 cards) → more cards after scrolling; end of list not observed.

Supplementary only: transient UI states, keyboard use, unusual input, stale state after refresh/Back, display oddities, ordering. Expected results stay Not established unless an observation supports them.
Two observed classes: no session (redirect to login) and authenticated session (Directory shown).
Card and panel content vary by employee data: all values present vs a value missing (location).
Only three filter dimensions with small value classes; the decision table (TA-004) covers the relevant combinations directly, so pairwise reduction is unnecessary.

techniques_used.rationale: The field accepts free text with distinct observed classes: matching partial, case variant, whitespace-padded, non-matching, typed-not-selected, selected suggestion, empty, overlong/special.

areas: PC SA-002/003/006 / filter controls: default vs set state
techniques_used.rationale: Controls have two observed classes (default '-- Select --'/empty vs a selected value); one representative per class covers the reset/default behavior.
Observed boundary in the header wording at result counts 0 ('No Records Found'), 1 ('(1) Record Found') and ≥2 ('(N) Records Found').
Search outcome depends on which of Employee Name, Job Title and Location are set and whether the name was selected.
Observed states closed → open (card click) → closed (arrow icon).
Observed states expanded → collapsed (toggle); the return transition was not evidenced.

areas: PC SA-002 / Employee Name validation message
techniques_used.rationale: Observed states: no message → 'Invalid' (Search with unselected text) → still 'Invalid' (retyping) → cleared (suggestion selected).
Observed states: initial batch (14 cards) → more cards after scrolling; end of list not observed.

Supplementary only: transient UI states, keyboard use, unusual input, stale state after refresh/Back, display oddities, ordering. Expected results stay Not established unless an observation supports them.
Two observed classes: no session (redirect to login) and authenticated session (Directory shown).
Card and panel content vary by employee data: all values present vs a value missing (location).
Only three filter dimensions with small value classes; the decision table (TA-004) covers the relevant combinations directly, so pairwise reduction is unnecessary.

trigger.user_message:
Run the required Test Review stage for the approved `TestCases.md` v1.1.0 and its matching `TestCases.csv`.

Review all 54 test cases for:
- Correctness and clear, repeatable test steps.
- Expected results supported by the approved PRD and exploration evidence.
- Positive, negative, boundary, validation, and combined-filter coverage.
- Missing, duplicate, overlapping, or unclear scenarios.
- Correct `valid in scope` and `needs automation` flags.
- Consistency between Markdown and CSV.

Important decisions:
- Directory UI only; no API testing.
- All 54 cases are in scope.
- TC-054 is the only automation case; the other 53 are manual-only.
- Demo data changes, so do not require fixed employee names or result counts.
- Treat uncertain behavior as exploratory; do not invent expected results.
- Do not modify approved files automatically. Report proposed corrections first.

Follow the existing Test Review workflow, record the review and evidence in the journal, and stop for my review. Do not execute tests or generate automation.

When finished, summarize findings by severity, list affected test case IDs, and wait for `TEST_REVIEW_APPROVED`.

review_findings.description: TC-017 – TC-019 type "the first 4 characters of the DATA-002 employee's first name", but DATA-002 only says the first name, "typed partially", yields exactly one suggestion. DATA-002 does not require the first name to have at least 4 characters, does not tie its uniqueness to the 4-character prefix used in the steps, and does not require an upper-case letter. The approved data includes an all-lower-case name ("yedghjb1 ru84 90jsnd", EVD-003), for which TC-018's lower-case partition is identical to TC-017. TC-014, TC-020, TC-021 and TC-024 type "part of" the name with no length at all.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: steps must be executable and use a concrete value or DATA-### (TestCases §4 rules; skill Test Case Generation Rules). DATA-002 (TestCases §10) vs steps of TC-017 – TC-019.
review_findings.proposed_change: Redefine DATA-002 (TestCases §10): first name of at least 4 characters, containing at least one upper-case letter, whose first-4-character prefix yields exactly one suggestion. Use the same prefix ("first 4 characters") in TC-014, TC-020, TC-021 and TC-024.
review_findings.reason: Two testers can choose different names or prefixes; with a short or lower-case name TC-017 cannot be performed as written and TC-018 tests nothing distinct, so a PASS would not be trustworthy.

review_findings.description: These cases "Search for the DATA-00x employee" (select the name suggestion, click Search) and then inspect "the result card" or "the card". DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 do not require a unique full name. The approved exploration shows several employees with the same full name (repeated "Linda Anderson", OBS-021, EVD-002). TC-020 expects "exactly one result card", but DATA-002's uniqueness covers the prefix, not the full name.
review_findings.basis: OBS-021 / EVD-002 (duplicate full names in the demo data); test-design rule: preconditions must set up the state the case needs (TestCases §4).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add to DATA-002, DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 (TestCases §10): the employee's full name appears exactly once in the suggestion list. Or change the steps so that the card is identified without a name search (e.g. via a Location filter and the card text).
review_findings.reason: With a duplicated name, the search returns several cards: TC-020 fails for a data reason, not an application reason, and the other cases inspect an arbitrary card.

review_findings.description: TC-011 and TC-054 need "a Job Title and a Location that together return at least one card (DATA-003 / DATA-004 pair)". DATA-003 and DATA-004 are defined separately (each returns at least one card); no DATA item defines a pair that returns a card together, or how to find one. TC-054 is the only automation case.
review_findings.basis: TestCases §10 (DATA-003, DATA-004); test-design Test Data Rules (data the environment must contain is stated as a precondition requirement).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add a DATA item (e.g. DATA-012): a Job Title + Location pair taken from one existing result card that shows both values, chosen at execution time. Reference it in TC-011 and TC-054 instead of the DATA-003 / DATA-004 pair.
review_findings.reason: Independently chosen values can return no cards; TC-011 then has no cards to check and TC-054 cannot complete step 2. For the automation case this makes the run non-deterministic.

review_findings.description: ExplorationReport §13 lists U-07 "Names with several matches (suggestion list ordering and limits)". TestCases.md has no case, TQ or CG for it; all other §13 limits (U-01 – U-06, U-08 – U-15 and the four unfinished flows) are carried into a case, TQ or CG.
review_findings.basis: Coverage Rules: Exploration §13 coverage limits are carried into Coverage Gaps; review check 1 floor (a §13 limit with neither a case, TQ nor CG).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add an Exploratory case and TQ for a name prefix with several matching employees (ordering and maximum number of suggestions), or add a CG explaining why it is not covered.
review_findings.reason: The source has neither a case nor a CG, so missing coverage is hidden.

review_findings.description: TC-036's Expected Result Basis is "OBS-008 + OBS-021 (observed baseline; human decision, journal EVT-0016)". OBS-021 is classified QUESTION. The human decision recorded in EVT-0016 adopts evidenced GAP-class observations as baseline; it does not cover QUESTION observations, which the Expected Result Rules map to Not established.
review_findings.basis: Test-design Expected Result Rules (QUESTION → Not established / Exploratory); human decision scope (EVT-0016 decisions[0]).
review_findings.proposed_change: TC-036 Expected Result Basis: cite OBS-008 only (it shows the "(2) Records Found" format). Keep OBS-021 in Traceability as context.
review_findings.reason: An expected result must rest only on an approved basis; the basis line is what Test Review and execution trust.

review_findings.description: TC-003 expects the URL to load AND the sidebar item to be active. TC-041 expects the panel to open AND the URL to stay the same. TC-045 expects the panel to close AND the URL to stay the same. Each pair is two independent observable outcomes; one can hold while the other fails.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: one single unambiguous expected result; independent expectations become separate cases.
review_findings.proposed_change: Split each into separate cases (new IDs), or move the URL check into its own case: e.g. TC-041 keeps "panel opens", a new case asserts "URL unchanged after card click"; TC-003 keeps one of URL / active item.
review_findings.reason: A FAIL would not show which expectation failed, and a partial result cannot be recorded as one PASS/FAIL.

review_findings.description: TC-036 expects "N is the number of matching records and N ≥ 2", but gives no way to count the matching records. Results load incrementally (OBS-019: 14 cards first), so for N > 14 a tester must scroll to count, and another may not.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: steps executable and deterministic where possible; OBS-019 (incremental loading).
review_findings.proposed_change: Constrain DATA-004 for TC-036 to a Location that returns between 2 and 14 records, and state the check: N equals the number of rendered cards.
review_findings.reason: Two testers could judge the same screen differently.

review_findings.description: All 37 established cases rest on observed behavior adopted by human decision (EVT-0016), recorded as assumption TA-AS-001 (Unconfirmed). This is stated openly in TestCases §2 and §3.
review_findings.basis: PC GAP-001 (no documented Directory behavior), PC RK-002 (a defect could be recorded as expected behavior).
review_findings.proposed_change: No change to cases. Recommended: a ProjectContext revision that documents the adopted behaviors, so later reviews judge them against documentation.
review_findings.reason: Sanctioned by a human decision, so it does not block; it remains a risk worth closing.

review_findings.description: TC-037 step 2 says "Scroll down inside the results area several times".
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: ordered, executable steps.
review_findings.proposed_change: State the action: scroll inside the results area until the last rendered card is visible, then wait for loading.
review_findings.reason: The outcome is unlikely to differ, but the step should be reproducible.

review_findings.description: DATA-006 says "verify no suggestion appears before use", which is what TC-026 itself asserts.
review_findings.basis: TestCases §10 DATA-006; OBS-017 (exploration used 'zzqxv').
review_findings.proposed_change: Define DATA-006 as a fixed design string (e.g. the value used in exploration, EVD-022) and remove the pre-verification.
review_findings.reason: Does not change how the result is judged.

review_findings.description: TC-004 is typed Business Rule with basis PC BR-006, but PC BR-006 is a QA-process rule (verify controls before finalizing scope), already met by exploration; the expected control set comes from OBS-004. Separately, the §5 matrix links PC DEP-006 only to TC-001, although every case uses DATA-001.
review_findings.basis: PC BR-006 text; TestCases §5 and §10.
review_findings.proposed_change: Type TC-004 as Positive (keep PC BR-006 in traceability as context). Add the other DATA-001 cases to the PC DEP-006 row, or note that all cases depend on it.
review_findings.reason: The link can be inferred, and the expected result is still supported by OBS-004.

review_findings.description: TC-054 (the only automation case) logs in with DATA-001, whose source is "credentials displayed on the application's login page". An automated run needs a configured, named secret source.
review_findings.basis: CLAUDE.md Secrets Rule; PC BR-016.
review_findings.proposed_change: For automation, name a configured test-data / secret source for DATA-001 (e.g. environment variables) without recording values.
review_findings.reason: Manual execution is unaffected; automation-generation will need it.

review_findings.description: TC-013 asks the tester to "immediately observe the toast area"; in exploration the toast had already gone when the screenshot was taken (OBS-011).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add: record the screen (or take a screenshot right after clicking Search) to capture the toast.
review_findings.reason: Evidence capture, not the expected result.

review_findings.description: ProjectContext §7 documents PC DEP-001 – DEP-009. TestCases.md traces only PC DEP-006; PC DEP-001 – DEP-005 and DEP-007 – DEP-009 appear in no case, matrix row or CG. PC DEP-001 / DEP-002 (OrangeHRM UI and Directory page available) are in practice exercised by TC-001 / TC-002, but this is not recorded.
review_findings.basis: Review check 1 floor: a documented dependency (PC DEP) with neither a covering case nor a CG.
review_findings.proposed_change: Add PC DEP-001 and DEP-002 to the traceability of TC-001 / TC-002 (and the §5 matrix); add a CG for the process dependencies DEP-003 – DEP-005 and DEP-007 – DEP-009 (PRD, scope, flags, Playwright, Claude, IntelliJ).
review_findings.reason: Without it, dependency coverage cannot be verified from the artifact.

Requirements:

1. Fix the test data for employee-name searches so the required prefix is at least four characters and produces an appropriate suggestion. Ensure the lowercase test is meaningful.
2. Ensure employee-name test cases can identify the intended employee unambiguously, even when names are duplicated.
3. Define a valid Job Title + Location pair from an observed employee card and use it in TC-011 and TC-054. Do not hardcode unstable employee names or result counts.

Preserve these decisions:
- Directory UI only; no API testing.
- All existing test cases remain in scope unless a specific change is necessary to resolve a finding.
- TC-054 is the ONLY case with `needs automation = TRUE`.
- All other cases must remain `needs automation = FALSE`.
- Demo data can change; do not rely on fixed employee names or total record counts.
- Keep uncertain behavior exploratory and do not invent expected results.

Update `TestCases.md` and `TestCases.csv` consistently. Preserve existing case IDs where possible; if new cases are required, assign unique IDs and update counts and traceability accordingly.

Run all existing test-design validations, verify the CSV and Markdown match, and record the revision in the journal. Do not execute tests or generate automation code.

review_findings.description: TC-017 – TC-019 type "the first 4 characters of the DATA-002 employee's first name", but DATA-002 only says the first name, "typed partially", yields exactly one suggestion. DATA-002 does not require the first name to have at least 4 characters, does not tie its uniqueness to the 4-character prefix used in the steps, and does not require an upper-case letter. The approved data includes an all-lower-case name ("yedghjb1 ru84 90jsnd", EVD-003), for which TC-018's lower-case partition is identical to TC-017. TC-014, TC-020, TC-021 and TC-024 type "part of" the name with no length at all.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: steps must be executable and use a concrete value or DATA-### (TestCases §4 rules; skill Test Case Generation Rules). DATA-002 (TestCases §10) vs steps of TC-017 – TC-019.
review_findings.proposed_change: Redefine DATA-002 (TestCases §10): first name of at least 4 characters, containing at least one upper-case letter, whose first-4-character prefix yields exactly one suggestion. Use the same prefix ("first 4 characters") in TC-014, TC-020, TC-021 and TC-024.
review_findings.reason: Two testers can choose different names or prefixes; with a short or lower-case name TC-017 cannot be performed as written and TC-018 tests nothing distinct, so a PASS would not be trustworthy.

resolution.reference: TestCases.md v1.2.0 (SHA-256 f61b7505…291a), TEST_DESIGN_APPROVED journal EVT-0023; produced by test-design EVT-0022

review_findings.description: These cases "Search for the DATA-00x employee" (select the name suggestion, click Search) and then inspect "the result card" or "the card". DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 do not require a unique full name. The approved exploration shows several employees with the same full name (repeated "Linda Anderson", OBS-021, EVD-002). TC-020 expects "exactly one result card", but DATA-002's uniqueness covers the prefix, not the full name.
review_findings.basis: OBS-021 / EVD-002 (duplicate full names in the demo data); test-design rule: preconditions must set up the state the case needs (TestCases §4).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add to DATA-002, DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 (TestCases §10): the employee's full name appears exactly once in the suggestion list. Or change the steps so that the card is identified without a name search (e.g. via a Location filter and the card text).
review_findings.reason: With a duplicated name, the search returns several cards: TC-020 fails for a data reason, not an application reason, and the other cases inspect an arbitrary card.

resolution.reference: TestCases.md v1.2.0 (SHA-256 f61b7505…291a), TEST_DESIGN_APPROVED journal EVT-0023; produced by test-design EVT-0022

review_findings.proposed_change: Add a DATA item (e.g. DATA-012): a Job Title + Location pair taken from one existing result card that shows both values, chosen at execution time. Reference it in TC-011 and TC-054 instead of the DATA-003 / DATA-004 pair.

review_findings.description: TC-054 (the only automation case) expects the results header to show the unfiltered "(N) Records Found" list after Reset, but no step records a reference count, and DATA-012 does not require the pair to return fewer records than the unfiltered list. A tester who only checks the "(N) Records Found" format would pass a Reset that clears the fields but leaves the filtered results. A tester who compares N with the count shown after login may fail the case because the shared data changes during a session (OBS-021: 130 → 141 in 10 minutes). The case also does not say when to read the header; a transient "No Records Found" was seen once while the list loaded (OBS-022, PB-001, unconfirmed). Not raised in review v1.0.0; found on this full re-run of the checks.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rules: executable, deterministic steps and one unambiguous expected result (TestCases §4 rules; skill Test Case Generation Rules). OBS-012 (Reset reloads the unfiltered results), OBS-021 (data changes during a session). TC-015 already handles the same check with a within-case comparison.
review_findings.proposed_change: TC-054: after the Search in step 2, note the filtered count k from the results header; change the results-header part of the Expected Result to "(N) Records Found with N greater than k", the TC-015 pattern (basis OBS-012). DATA-012: add "the pair returns fewer records than the unfiltered list", as DATA-004 does for TC-015. Also recommended: state that the header is read once the result cards are displayed after Reset (PB-001 stays explored by TC-050).
review_findings.reason: As written, two testers can reach different verdicts on the same screen, and automation-generation would have to invent the "unfiltered" assertion, which the platform forbids. TC-054 is the only automation case. Where it is unclear whether a result could become untrustworthy, the rule is Change Required.

review_findings.description: §1 Revision History: the 1.0.0 row lists "TC-001…TC-058" as added, but v1.0.0 had 54 cases; TC-055 – TC-058 were added in 1.2.0, as the 1.2.0 row correctly says. §3 still says the cases already FALSE include "Exploratory (17)", while §11 and §4 have 18 Exploratory cases (TC-055 is new). §2 Constraints say data is chosen at execution time from "DATA-002 – DATA-010", although DATA-012 – DATA-015 are also execution-time data.
review_findings.basis: Internal consistency of TestCases.md (§1 and §3 vs §4 and §11; §2 vs §10).
review_findings.proposed_change: §1: change the 1.0.0 row's Added column to TC-001…TC-054. §3: "Exploratory (18)". §2: refer to DATA-002 – DATA-015 (excluding DATA-006 and DATA-011, which are design values), or to "the DATA items in §10".
review_findings.reason: The §11 counts, which the traceability check relies on, match §4, so no case is performed or judged differently. The stale text could mislead a reader of the revision history.

review_findings.description: DATA-013 confirms uniqueness by checking that the full name appears exactly once in the suggestion list for the 4-character prefix. Whether that list is truncated is unknown (TQ-016, TC-055). DATA-002 limits the list by requiring a prefix that begins no other displayed card's first name, but DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 have no such condition, so a common prefix could produce a truncated list that hides a same-named employee.
review_findings.basis: TQ-016 (suggestion-list length and truncation not observed); OBS-021 (duplicate names in the demo data); DATA-002 vs DATA-007 / DATA-008 / DATA-009 (TestCases §10).
review_findings.proposed_change: Require DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 employees to also meet DATA-002's prefix condition (the 4-character prefix begins no other displayed card's first name), or revisit DATA-013 once TQ-016 is answered.
review_findings.reason: The residual risk is small, and a hidden duplicate would show as two identically named cards, visible to the tester rather than silently changing a verdict.

trigger.reason: Human requested execution of TC-001 – TC-058 via Playwright MCP
trigger.user_message:
Execute the complete OrangeHRM Directory test suite (TC-001 to TC-058) interactively in front of me using Playwright MCP.

## 1. Inspect the existing workflow
- Inspect the existing project skills, agents, Playwright MCP setup, Test Design v1.3.0, and execution artifacts.
- Reuse the existing Manual Test Execution skill if available. Otherwise, create a reusable skill following the project's conventions.
- Do not spend time on another review cycle before execution.

## 2. Execute visibly in the browser
- Open the actual OrangeHRM Directory application using Playwright MCP.
- Keep the browser visible so I can watch the execution live.
- Execute every test case from TC-001 through TC-058 in ID order, following its actual steps and expected results.
- Use the real application UI and current demo data. Do not simulate execution, fabricate results, or hard-code employee names or record counts.
- Execute positive, negative, validation, boundary, and other applicable scenarios.
- Reset the application state between cases when necessary.
- If the browser becomes unavailable or a case is blocked, document the reason and continue with independent cases whenever possible.
- Do not stop after TC-054. TC-054 remains the only case marked for automation in Test Design, but all 58 cases must receive genuine execution attempts.

## 3. Record execution results
For every test case, record:
- Test Case ID and title
- Actual result
- Status: Pass, Fail, Blocked, or Not Executed
- Execution notes
- Evidence, such as screenshots or relevant browser observations, where available

Never mark a test as passed unless its expected result was actually verified.

## 4. Create a Problem Review Report FIRST
Before creating any bug reports, consolidate all observed failures and suspicious behavior in a separate review artifact, for example `ExecutionProblemReview.md`.

For each finding, record:
- Finding ID
- Related Test Case ID
- Expected versus actual behavior
- Reproduction steps
- Evidence
- Initial assessment: Confirmed Failure, Suspected Issue, or Environment/Test Data Issue
- Missing information or further verification needed

Separate confirmed failures from unconfirmed observations. Do not automatically treat every failed test as an application bug.

## 5. Review findings before creating bugs
After execution and the Problem Review Report are complete:
- Stop and show me the report and execution summary.
- Do not create formal bug reports yet.
- Wait for my review and explicit approval of the findings.

## 6. Create bugs after my approval
Once I approve the findings, create formal bug reports only for the approved, sufficiently evidenced application defects. Each bug must include:
- Unique Bug ID
- Clear title
- Environment and preconditions
- Reproduction steps
- Expected result
- Actual result
- Severity and priority, with rationale
- Related Test Case ID
- Evidence
- Reproducibility status

Do not create duplicate bugs for the same root issue.

## 7. Project integrity
- Keep Directory UI testing as the scope; API testing is excluded.
- Preserve the existing Test Design and historical journal entries.
- Append new journal events instead of editing old ones.
- Update the execution report and all 58 case statuses accurately.
- Do not approve Test Design or Test Review automatically.
- Do not claim execution or evidence that did not actually occur.

Start now by inspecting the existing workflow, then open the visible browser and begin executing the test cases. Show me the execution as it happens, and stop for my review before creating formal bug reports.

review_findings.description: TC-017 – TC-019 type "the first 4 characters of the DATA-002 employee's first name", but DATA-002 only says the first name, "typed partially", yields exactly one suggestion. DATA-002 does not require the first name to have at least 4 characters, does not tie its uniqueness to the 4-character prefix used in the steps, and does not require an upper-case letter. The approved data includes an all-lower-case name ("yedghjb1 ru84 90jsnd", EVD-003), for which TC-018's lower-case partition is identical to TC-017. TC-014, TC-020, TC-021 and TC-024 type "part of" the name with no length at all.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: steps must be executable and use a concrete value or DATA-### (TestCases §4 rules; skill Test Case Generation Rules). DATA-002 (TestCases §10) vs steps of TC-017 – TC-019.
review_findings.proposed_change: Redefine DATA-002 (TestCases §10): first name of at least 4 characters, containing at least one upper-case letter, whose first-4-character prefix yields exactly one suggestion. Use the same prefix ("first 4 characters") in TC-014, TC-020, TC-021 and TC-024.
review_findings.reason: Two testers can choose different names or prefixes; with a short or lower-case name TC-017 cannot be performed as written and TC-018 tests nothing distinct, so a PASS would not be trustworthy.

resolution.reference: TestCases.md v1.2.0 (SHA-256 f61b7505…291a), TEST_DESIGN_APPROVED journal EVT-0023; produced by test-design EVT-0022

review_findings.description: These cases "Search for the DATA-00x employee" (select the name suggestion, click Search) and then inspect "the result card" or "the card". DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 do not require a unique full name. The approved exploration shows several employees with the same full name (repeated "Linda Anderson", OBS-021, EVD-002). TC-020 expects "exactly one result card", but DATA-002's uniqueness covers the prefix, not the full name.
review_findings.basis: OBS-021 / EVD-002 (duplicate full names in the demo data); test-design rule: preconditions must set up the state the case needs (TestCases §4).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add to DATA-002, DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 (TestCases §10): the employee's full name appears exactly once in the suggestion list. Or change the steps so that the card is identified without a name search (e.g. via a Location filter and the card text).
review_findings.reason: With a duplicated name, the search returns several cards: TC-020 fails for a data reason, not an application reason, and the other cases inspect an arbitrary card.

review_findings.description: TC-011 and TC-054 need "a Job Title and a Location that together return at least one card (DATA-003 / DATA-004 pair)". DATA-003 and DATA-004 are defined separately (each returns at least one card); no DATA item defines a pair that returns a card together, or how to find one. TC-054 is the only automation case.
review_findings.basis: TestCases §10 (DATA-003, DATA-004); test-design Test Data Rules (data the environment must contain is stated as a precondition requirement).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add a DATA item (e.g. DATA-012): a Job Title + Location pair taken from one existing result card that shows both values, chosen at execution time. Reference it in TC-011 and TC-054 instead of the DATA-003 / DATA-004 pair.
review_findings.reason: Independently chosen values can return no cards; TC-011 then has no cards to check and TC-054 cannot complete step 2. For the automation case this makes the run non-deterministic.

review_findings.description: TC-003 expects the URL to load AND the sidebar item to be active. TC-041 expects the panel to open AND the URL to stay the same. TC-045 expects the panel to close AND the URL to stay the same. Each pair is two independent observable outcomes; one can hold while the other fails.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: one single unambiguous expected result; independent expectations become separate cases.
review_findings.proposed_change: Split each into separate cases (new IDs), or move the URL check into its own case: e.g. TC-041 keeps "panel opens", a new case asserts "URL unchanged after card click"; TC-003 keeps one of URL / active item.
review_findings.reason: A FAIL would not show which expectation failed, and a partial result cannot be recorded as one PASS/FAIL.

review_findings.description: TC-054 (the only automation case) expects the results header to show the unfiltered "(N) Records Found" list after Reset, but no step records a reference count, and DATA-012 does not require the pair to return fewer records than the unfiltered list. A tester who only checks the "(N) Records Found" format would pass a Reset that clears the fields but leaves the filtered results. A tester who compares N with the count shown after login may fail the case because the shared data changes during a session (OBS-021: 130 → 141 in 10 minutes). The case also does not say when to read the header; a transient "No Records Found" was seen once while the list loaded (OBS-022, PB-001, unconfirmed). Not raised in review v1.0.0; found on this full re-run of the checks.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rules: executable, deterministic steps and one unambiguous expected result (TestCases §4 rules; skill Test Case Generation Rules). OBS-012 (Reset reloads the unfiltered results), OBS-021 (data changes during a session). TC-015 already handles the same check with a within-case comparison.
review_findings.proposed_change: TC-054: after the Search in step 2, note the filtered count k from the results header; change the results-header part of the Expected Result to "(N) Records Found with N greater than k", the TC-015 pattern (basis OBS-012). DATA-012: add "the pair returns fewer records than the unfiltered list", as DATA-004 does for TC-015. Also recommended: state that the header is read once the result cards are displayed after Reset (PB-001 stays explored by TC-050).
review_findings.reason: As written, two testers can reach different verdicts on the same screen, and automation-generation would have to invent the "unfiltered" assertion, which the platform forbids. TC-054 is the only automation case. Where it is unclear whether a result could become untrustworthy, the rule is Change Required.

review_findings.basis: Internal consistency of TestCases.md (§1 and §3 vs §4 and §11; §2 vs §10).
review_findings.proposed_change: §1: change the 1.0.0 row's Added column to TC-001…TC-054. §3: "Exploratory (18)". §2: refer to DATA-002 – DATA-015 (excluding DATA-006 and DATA-011, which are design values), or to "the DATA items in §10".
review_findings.reason: The §11 counts, which the traceability check relies on, match §4, so no case is performed or judged differently. The stale text could mislead a reader of the revision history.

review_findings.description: DATA-013 confirms uniqueness by checking that the full name appears exactly once in the suggestion list for the 4-character prefix. Whether that list is truncated is unknown (TQ-016, TC-055). DATA-002 limits the list by requiring a prefix that begins no other displayed card's first name, but DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 have no such condition, so a common prefix could produce a truncated list that hides a same-named employee.
review_findings.basis: TQ-016 (suggestion-list length and truncation not observed); OBS-021 (duplicate names in the demo data); DATA-002 vs DATA-007 / DATA-008 / DATA-009 (TestCases §10).
review_findings.proposed_change: Require DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 employees to also meet DATA-002's prefix condition (the 4-character prefix begins no other displayed card's first name), or revisit DATA-013 once TQ-016 is answered.
review_findings.reason: The residual risk is small, and a hidden duplicate would show as two identically named cards, visible to the tester rather than silently changing a verdict.

trigger.user_message:
Execute the complete OrangeHRM Directory test suite (TC-001 to TC-058) interactively in front of me using Playwright MCP.

## 1. Inspect the existing workflow
- Inspect the existing project skills, agents, Playwright MCP setup, Test Design v1.3.0, and execution artifacts.
- Reuse the existing Manual Test Execution skill if available. Otherwise, create a reusable skill following the project's conventions.
- Do not spend time on another review cycle before execution.

## 2. Execute visibly in the browser
- Open the actual OrangeHRM Directory application using Playwright MCP.
- Keep the browser visible so I can watch the execution live.
- Execute every test case from TC-001 through TC-058 in ID order, following its actual steps and expected results.
- Use the real application UI and current demo data. Do not simulate execution, fabricate results, or hard-code employee names or record counts.
- Execute positive, negative, validation, boundary, and other applicable scenarios.
- Reset the application state between cases when necessary.
- If the browser becomes unavailable or a case is blocked, document the reason and continue with independent cases whenever possible.
- Do not stop after TC-054. TC-054 remains the only case marked for automation in Test Design, but all 58 cases must receive genuine execution attempts.

## 3. Record execution results
For every test case, record:
- Test Case ID and title
- Actual result
- Status: Pass, Fail, Blocked, or Not Executed
- Execution notes
- Evidence, such as screenshots or relevant browser observations, where available

Never mark a test as passed unless its expected result was actually verified.

## 4. Create a Problem Review Report FIRST
Before creating any bug reports, consolidate all observed failures and suspicious behavior in a separate review artifact, for example `ExecutionProblemReview.md`.

For each finding, record:
- Finding ID
- Related Test Case ID
- Expected versus actual behavior
- Reproduction steps
- Evidence
- Initial assessment: Confirmed Failure, Suspected Issue, or Environment/Test Data Issue
- Missing information or further verification needed

Separate confirmed failures from unconfirmed observations. Do not automatically treat every failed test as an application bug.

## 5. Review findings before creating bugs
After execution and the Problem Review Report are complete:
- Stop and show me the report and execution summary.
- Do not create formal bug reports yet.
- Wait for my review and explicit approval of the findings.

## 6. Create bugs after my approval
Once I approve the findings, create formal bug reports only for the approved, sufficiently evidenced application defects. Each bug must include:
- Unique Bug ID
- Clear title
- Environment and preconditions
- Reproduction steps
- Expected result
- Actual result
- Severity and priority, with rationale
- Related Test Case ID
- Evidence
- Reproducibility status

Do not create duplicate bugs for the same root issue.

1. Treat every suspected application defect in `ExecutionProblemReview.md` as a candidate bug. Create a bug report for every suspected issue, including PR-001 through PR-005, using the available evidence.
2. Clearly label each issue as Confirmed or Suspected. Do not present unverified behavior as a confirmed defect.
3. Include the finding ID, related test case, reproduction steps, expected versus actual behavior, evidence, severity, and priority. If the expected behavior is not documented, explicitly state "Expected behavior requires confirmation" rather than inventing a requirement.
4. Keep environment and test-data issues PR-006 through PR-008 in a separate section; do not report them as application bugs unless evidence supports that classification.
5. Include the new TC-024 finding in the review notes and retain its evidence.
6. Update `bugs/BugReports.md` and any existing bug registry or index consistently. Preserve all previous execution results and append journal events without rewriting history.
7. Do not spend time resolving all 18 exploratory questions before creating candidate bug reports.
8. Do not rerun tests unless a minimal verification is necessary. Do not fabricate test results or evidence.
9. Show me a concise summary of the bug reports created and any unresolved limitations.

After documenting the suspected bugs, stop. Do not perform Git operations or push anything yet.

review_findings.description: TC-017 – TC-019 type "the first 4 characters of the DATA-002 employee's first name", but DATA-002 only says the first name, "typed partially", yields exactly one suggestion. DATA-002 does not require the first name to have at least 4 characters, does not tie its uniqueness to the 4-character prefix used in the steps, and does not require an upper-case letter. The approved data includes an all-lower-case name ("yedghjb1 ru84 90jsnd", EVD-003), for which TC-018's lower-case partition is identical to TC-017. TC-014, TC-020, TC-021 and TC-024 type "part of" the name with no length at all.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: steps must be executable and use a concrete value or DATA-### (TestCases §4 rules; skill Test Case Generation Rules). DATA-002 (TestCases §10) vs steps of TC-017 – TC-019.
review_findings.proposed_change: Redefine DATA-002 (TestCases §10): first name of at least 4 characters, containing at least one upper-case letter, whose first-4-character prefix yields exactly one suggestion. Use the same prefix ("first 4 characters") in TC-014, TC-020, TC-021 and TC-024.
review_findings.reason: Two testers can choose different names or prefixes; with a short or lower-case name TC-017 cannot be performed as written and TC-018 tests nothing distinct, so a PASS would not be trustworthy.

resolution.reference: TestCases.md v1.2.0 (SHA-256 f61b7505…291a), TEST_DESIGN_APPROVED journal EVT-0023; produced by test-design EVT-0022

review_findings.description: These cases "Search for the DATA-00x employee" (select the name suggestion, click Search) and then inspect "the result card" or "the card". DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 do not require a unique full name. The approved exploration shows several employees with the same full name (repeated "Linda Anderson", OBS-021, EVD-002). TC-020 expects "exactly one result card", but DATA-002's uniqueness covers the prefix, not the full name.
review_findings.basis: OBS-021 / EVD-002 (duplicate full names in the demo data); test-design rule: preconditions must set up the state the case needs (TestCases §4).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add to DATA-002, DATA-007, DATA-008 and DATA-009 (TestCases §10): the employee's full name appears exactly once in the suggestion list. Or change the steps so that the card is identified without a name search (e.g. via a Location filter and the card text).
review_findings.reason: With a duplicated name, the search returns several cards: TC-020 fails for a data reason, not an application reason, and the other cases inspect an arbitrary card.

review_findings.description: TC-011 and TC-054 need "a Job Title and a Location that together return at least one card (DATA-003 / DATA-004 pair)". DATA-003 and DATA-004 are defined separately (each returns at least one card); no DATA item defines a pair that returns a card together, or how to find one. TC-054 is the only automation case.
review_findings.basis: TestCases §10 (DATA-003, DATA-004); test-design Test Data Rules (data the environment must contain is stated as a precondition requirement).
review_findings.proposed_change: Add a DATA item (e.g. DATA-012): a Job Title + Location pair taken from one existing result card that shows both values, chosen at execution time. Reference it in TC-011 and TC-054 instead of the DATA-003 / DATA-004 pair.
review_findings.reason: Independently chosen values can return no cards; TC-011 then has no cards to check and TC-054 cannot complete step 2. For the automation case this makes the run non-deterministic.

review_findings.description: TC-003 expects the URL to load AND the sidebar item to be active. TC-041 expects the panel to open AND the URL to stay the same. TC-045 expects the panel to close AND the URL to stay the same. Each pair is two independent observable outcomes; one can hold while the other fails.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rule: one single unambiguous expected result; independent expectations become separate cases.
review_findings.proposed_change: Split each into separate cases (new IDs), or move the URL check into its own case: e.g. TC-041 keeps "panel opens", a new case asserts "URL unchanged after card click"; TC-003 keeps one of URL / active item.
review_findings.reason: A FAIL would not show which expectation failed, and a partial result cannot be recorded as one PASS/FAIL.

review_findings.description: TC-054 (the only automation case) expects the results header to show the unfiltered "(N) Records Found" list after Reset, but no step records a reference count, and DATA-012 does not require the pair to return fewer records than the unfiltered list. A tester who only checks the "(N) Records Found" format would pass a Reset that clears the fields but leaves the filtered results. A tester who compares N with the count shown after login may fail the case because the shared data changes during a session (OBS-021: 130 → 141 in 10 minutes). The case also does not say when to read the header; a transient "No Records Found" was seen once while the list loaded (OBS-022, PB-001, unconfirmed). Not raised in review v1.0.0; found on this full re-run of the checks.
review_findings.basis: Test-design rules: executable, deterministic steps and one unambiguous expected result (TestCases §4 rules; skill Test Case Generation Rules). OBS-012 (Reset reloads the unfiltered results), OBS-021 (data changes during a session). TC-015 already handles the same check with a within-case comparison.
review_findings.proposed_change: TC-054: after the Search in step 2, note the filtered count k from the results header; change the results-header part of the Expected Result to "(N) Records Found with N greater than k", the TC-015 pattern (basis OBS-012). DATA-012: add "the pair returns fewer records than the unfiltered list", as DATA-004 does for TC-015. Also recommended: state that the header is read once the result cards are displayed after Reset (PB-001 stays explored by TC-050).
review_findings.reason: As written, two testers can reach different verdicts on the same screen, and automation-generation would have to invent the "unfiltered" assertion, which the platform forbids. TC-054 is the only automation case. Where it is unclear whether a result could become untrustworthy, the rule is Change Required.
